title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
statement:
You are given a string `s` of length `n` made only of uppercase and lowercase English letters (`A`-`Z` and `a`-`z`; the two cases are **different** characters), and an integer `k` with `0 < k < n`.

You may make **at most `k` changes**: in one change you pick any position of the string and replace its letter with any other letter. After the changes, look for a **substring** (a contiguous block of characters) in which all characters are the same.

Print the **maximum possible length** of such a substring, over all choices of at most `k` changes.
input_format:
The first line contains the string `s`.
The second line contains the integer `k`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the length of the longest substring of one repeated letter that can be obtained with at most `k` changes.
constraints: s contains only the letters A-Z and a-z

examples.explanation: Change the two `B`s into `A`s (or the two `A`s into `B`s). The whole string becomes `AAAA`, so the answer is 4.
Replace the middle `B` in `AABA` so the block becomes `AAAA`, length 4. No window of length 5 has at most one letter different from its most common letter.
`a` and `A` are different letters. Changing one `A` to `a` gives `aaaA` or `aAaa`, so the longest block of equal letters has length 3.

hints: A window of length L can be made uniform with at most k changes exactly when L minus the count of its most frequent letter is at most k.
Use two pointers. Expand the right end, track the counts of letters inside the window, and shrink from the left when the window needs more than k changes.
You do not have to recompute the maximum frequency when shrinking: the window never needs to get smaller than the best length found so far, so a stale maximum is safe.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    s = data[0]
    k = int(data[1])
    cnt = {}
    best = 0
    left = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        cnt[ch] = cnt.get(ch, 0) + 1
        best = max(best, cnt[ch])
        if right - left + 1 - best > k:
            cnt[s[left]] -= 1
            left += 1
    print(len(s) - left)

main()

ans = 0

    for i in range(n):
        bad = 0
        for j in range(i, n):
            if s[j] != c:
                bad += 1
            if bad > k:
                break
            ans = max(ans, j - i + 1)
